paper_metadata.title: High toughness and high strength spray-deposited AlCuMgAg-base alloys for use at moderately elevated temperatures

evidence.quote: Chemical composition and heat treatments of spray-deposited AlCuMgAg-base alloys for use at ambient and moderately elevated temperatures have been optimized for high strength and high fracture toughness.
Two new spray-deposited AlCuMgAg-base alloys with excellent mechanical properties have been developed.
Alloy N213 (AlCu5Mg0.4Ag0.4Ti0.4Zr0.15Mn0.2) clearly outperforms commercial 2XXX series alloys such as 26 18 in terms of fracture toughness and yield strength at temperatures up to 180 “C.
Subsequently alloy N213 was peak aged at 180 “C for 12 h, whereas alloy N232 was peak aged at 165 “C for 20 h (T6 tempers).

Alloy N232 (AlCu4Mg0.8Ag0.4ZrOSMnO.4) shows the highest product of yield strength and fracture toughness ever achieved for aluminium alloys; at 23 “C yield strength and fracture toughness values are R,,,, = 378 MPa, K,, = 100 MPa ml’2 (T4 temper), and R PO.? = 452 MPa, K,, = 77 MPa ml’* (T6 temper).

Alloys N213 and N232 have been produced by spray deposition at Alusuisse-Lonza AG, Neuhausen, Switzerland. The spray-deposited billets had a diameter of approximately 220 mm and a mass up to 30 kg.
In a second step these preforms were preheated to 420 “C and processed by hot extrusion with a ratio of 21.5 to profiles with a cross-section of 70 mm x 25 mm.
Alloy N2 13 was solution heat treated at 525 “C for 2 h and then water quenched to room temperature.

A stable naturally aged condition (T4 temper) for alloy N213 was reached after more than 1000 h exposure at ambient temperature; this process could be considerably accelerated by aging at temperatures up to 120 “C.
Subsequently alloy N213 was peak aged at 180 “C for 12 h, whereas alloy N232 was peak aged at 165 “C for 20 h (T6 tempers).
